meaning: A public phone that lets you make a call after you pay with coins or a card.
clues: It is a telephone device used by many people.
You pay for each call, usually with coins or a card.
It can help when your own phone is not with you.
It stood in public places such as airports and hotels.
It has one word, with eight letters, and starts with P.
assumes: A switchboard connects callers through an operator
A party line is one phone line shared by several homes
A telegraph sends messages as taps on a key, not by voice

decoys.meaning: A panel where an operator joined callers with cords.
One phone line shared by several homes, so neighbors could pick up and hear each other's calls.
A machine that sends messages over a wire as short and long taps of a key, called Morse code.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: A public phone gave you a way to reach someone when you were out. Having a backup way to call still matters.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: your own cell phone. If the battery dies, ask a clerk at a shop or front desk for help placing a call.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Coins in your hand kept each call simple. You paid for the call, and that was the end of it.

sources.name: FCC, Tips for Using Public Phones and Payphones
